structured.answer: After 8 years, putting in the 500 ₪ a month the calculator suggested, I'd put in 48,000 and have about 68,853 ₪ with no tax. For 4 years the page gives no figure for self-employed people ("לעצמאים עוד אין כאן חישוב למשיכה לפני 6 שנים"), so I don't know. I'll ask my son or the bank, because the 7% is the site's own assumption on an "S&P500" track, not a safe deposit.

stuck.why: The only number shown, 25,725, sits over 'אותו כסף בחשבון ניירות ערך', not the fund. I almost took it as the 4-year answer before reading the orange note that there's no calculation for self-employed before 6 years.
The task gave no amount and I couldn't work out 20,566 a year as a monthly figure, so I left the 500 ₪ that was filled in.

findings.what: At 4 years the fund shows no figure. The only number on screen (25,725) belongs to a different account, which is easy to take as the answer.
The result is worked out on a share-index (S&P500) track at an assumed 7%. This only shows up in small notes below the chart, not next to the big number.
The text says 3 years is enough for people past retirement age, but the calculator ignores age and treats everything before 6 years as taxed or not calculated
The stacked bars use close colours (yellow, dark yellow, teal, dark teal) that are hard to tell apart
Dark background with grey text is tiring to read
The 500 ₪ monthly default has nothing to do with the 20,566 ₪ yearly limit mentioned above it
